themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in Bensonhurst/Bath Beach spiked to 37 THIS WEEK, a 448% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 6.8 per week (z-score: 8.33), suggesting a sudden, acute disruption affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 37 noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (448% spike)
Z-score of 8.33 indicates statistically severe deviation from baseline
Noise - Residential is the second-highest complaint category overall (2,670 complaints in 90 days), but this week's spike is abnormal
reporting_angles: Canvass affected residents and block captains to identify source(s): construction, venue opening, event, or other localized cause
Contact NYPD and DOE to request enforcement data for this week and confirm what triggered the spike

themes_detail.label: Emergency Response Team Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Emergency Response Team complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK, a 991% spike over the 8-week baseline of 1.4 per week (z-score: 12.26), signaling a sudden surge in 911 calls or police/EMS dispatch issues demanding immediate investigation.
evidence: 15 ERT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (991% increase)
Z-score of 12.26 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
This is the second-highest z-score spike in the entire dataset, behind only Building/Use violations
reporting_angles: Request FDNY and NYPD incident data for this week—what emergencies triggered the ERT callouts and why the sudden cluster?
Interview NYPD Community Affairs to learn if dispatch delays, crime, or a specific event drove the spike

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Use Violations Explode
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints surged to 87 LAST WEEK, a 709% spike over the 8-week baseline of 10.8 per week (z-score: 22.8), marking the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting widespread code violations or an enforcement crackdown.
evidence: 87 Building/Use complaints LAST WEEK vs. 10.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (709% spike)
Z-score of 22.8 is the highest anomaly across all complaint categories
507 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (418 alterations) suggest active construction activity that may correlate with violations
reporting_angles: Contact DOB to identify which addresses generated the spike—are violations concentrated in one area or dispersed? Are they alteration-related?
Request DOE and HPD enforcement records to determine if violations involve illegal conversions, overcrowding, or structural/safety issues

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 2300% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.1 per week (z-score: 8.69), indicating a sudden emergence of homelessness or informal settlements in the district.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
CB budget data shows recurring requests for mental health and outreach services, suggesting pre-existing vulnerable population
reporting_angles: Document the location and size of encampments—are they transit-adjacent (subway, bus terminal), park-based, or street-level?
Interview NYC Parks, Sanitation, and Police to understand outreach response and whether encampments are newly visible or newly established

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Collection Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 15 LAST WEEK, a 532% spike over the 8-week baseline of 2.4 per week (z-score: 7.63), suggesting either a public health event (disease outbreak, mass die-off) or a sanitation service failure.
evidence: 15 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (532% spike)
Aligns with CB budget request for sanitation infrastructure upgrades, suggesting underlying service gaps
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks and Sanitation to determine cause—disease outbreak (rat, pigeon, pest die-off), collection delays, or other factors
Verify if complaints are geographically clustered (waterfront, park, residential) or dispersed across the district
